  "text": "The library envelope arrived with six bean seeds and a card asking that some be returned after harvest.

Arthur put it beside his wife’s gardening gloves.

In April, he filled six pots. He pushed each seed into the compost with his thumb, then read the instructions and dug them up again. Too deep.

Five came through.

He rang his daughter to tell her.

“Is that good?” she asked.

“I don’t know yet.”

By June they had climbed the poles he’d found behind the shed. His wife had tied the poles in bundles with strips of old bedsheet. He used those strips again, though some tore when he pulled them tight.

There were more beans than he could eat. He left bags on two neighbours’ steps and learned to pick them before they grew stringy.

In September, he let the last pods dry on the vines.

At the kitchen table, he opened them over a newspaper. The beans were purple, speckled with cream. He counted forty-three.

The library card had a space for his name and another for notes.

He wrote: Five plants. Good crop.

Then he crossed out Good and wrote Heavy.

He put thirty seeds in an envelope. The others went into a tobacco tin, although he hadn’t smoked for twenty years.

At the library, the woman at the desk asked whether he wanted anything else.

“Not today,” he said.

Outside, he stopped beside the noticeboard. There was a photograph of a yellow climbing bean.

He went back to ask whether it needed different poles."
